text: Jben is the fresh cheese of the Maghreb: raw milk is set with rennet or left to curdle with its own lactic flora, the curd is ladled into cloth and drained, then salted and pressed into rounds. It is not ripened. Industrial versions use pasteurised milk, about 3 % starter and rennet added once the milk reaches 0.20–0.25 % lactic acid, with moulding at pH 4.4–4.6.

steps.note: Animal rennet (Ain Sefra: dried lamb or kid abomasum, "el Hakka"), calf rennet or a plant extract such as artichoke flower; home versions use lben.

processing.text: Traditionally the raw milk curdles with its own lactic flora; industrial versions use pasteurised milk with about 3 % starter, moulded at pH 4.4-4.6. Unripened, eaten within 10-15 days.
